In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between the constraints from the exclusive and inclusive decays, which are found to be complementary in nature.
the study of exclusive radiative B-mesons decays, which can provide additional information on the flavour alignment in the two-Higgs-double model, and thus on new sources of CP-violation.
the question whether exclusive B → Vγ decays can be used to probe the flavour alignment of Yukawa couplings in the two-Higgs-doublets model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, while the alignment of the Yukawa matrices is still a viable solution to the flavour problem of the SM, it is not the only one.
the current experimental data on B → V γ are in good agreement with the SM and the aligned two-Highgs-doublet model, with the exception of the isospin violation in B → K*γ decays.
the current data do not allow for an exclusion of new physics in the B → V γ sector, but that they also do not provide a significant hint for new physics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while exclusive B → Vγ and inclusive B →Xs,dγ decays are complementary to each other, the current data do not provide much information about the underlying physics.

the constraints on the new physics parameters are not significantly stronger than those obtained from the inclusive decays, and that there are no significant correlations between the exclusive and inclusive decays.
, within the aligned two-doublet model, a large part of the parameter space allowed by B → Xsγ is already excluded by the exclusive B → Vγ decays.
The main takeaway from our work is that
exclusive radiative B decays can provide important complementary constraints to the ones from inclusive B → X γ decays.

the alignment of the Yukawa couplings in flavour space, which is crucial in the two-Higgs-doublets model, does not necessarily imply that the new physics contributions to the radiative decays will be small.

the alignment of Yukawas in flavour space is not a necessary condition to explain the experimental data, and that the alignment can in fact be significantly relaxed, while still being able to accommodate the experimental data within 2 σ.
